chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'or what you possess the keys of, or your friends', he said: 'These are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named in this verse. They eat without their permission from the dates and the curries (food), and similarly the wife eats from the house of her husband without his permission. So as for what is besides that from the food, then no (permission is needed).'
ai.seo_question: Who can eat from your food without asking for permission according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the scope of the Quranic phrase 'or what you possess the keys of' (24:61), interpreting it as granting close friends and family the right to consume stored provisions like dates and main dishes without seeking explicit permission. This ruling parallels the domestic privilege of a wife eating from her husband's store, establishing a legal precedent for informal access to specific types of food within trusted circles, while maintaining the requirement of permission for other items. This interpretation highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on social intimacy and trust (*sadiq*) as factors that relax formal ownership boundaries regarding consumable goods.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Safwan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:61] or what you possess the keys of, or your friends' (houses), having said: ‘Those whom Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Named in this Verse eat without their permission, from the dates, and the curries; and similar to that is the food (eaten by) the wife from the house of her husband without his permission. So as for besides that from the foodstuff, so no’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ’. . . or the house to which you have the keys or your friend’, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The people Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has mentioned in this verse can eat without the permission of the owner of the house, things such as dates and curries and so also can a woman eat from the house of her husband without his permission. However, it is not permissible for them to eat other items of food besides the ones mentioned above.’”
